title: Superexponential strict-improvement distances in median graphs
shortTitle: When a better graph center is far away
oneLine: Integer separation forces very long strictly improving moves, even in median graphs.
abstract: This unrefereed candidate realizes minimum integer separation norm exactly as the distance to a strict radius improvement on a grid, then transfers the construction to ordinary eccentricity without increasing cube dimension. An explicit Fibonacci family disproves dimension-linear locality. An attributed Alon–Vũ theorem gives a superexponential lower bound in every sufficiently large dimension, with a matching leading logarithmic exponent for corner profiles. This is not an algorithmic running-time lower bound.

narration: Suppose you are looking for a central point in a network: a vertex whose greatest distance to any other vertex is as small as possible. A natural approach is to look nearby for a better choice. How far must you look before the absence of a strict improvement tells you that you have found a center? This candidate studies median graphs, a structured family that includes rectangular grids. It shows that cube dimension alone does not provide the proposed linear search radius. An explicit family requires a move whose length grows like a Fibonacci number before eccentricity strictly decreases. The construction connects two mathematical objects: integer solutions of separation inequalities, and distances from selected corners of a grid. Adding paths at those corners converts the example into ordinary, unweighted graph eccentricity. Combining this transfer with an established theorem of Alon and Vu gives a stronger, superexponential obstruction in every sufficiently large dimension. A complementary bound identifies the leading logarithmic scale for the restricted corner-profile model. The distinction is strict improvement. Equal-value moves can sometimes lead to a later decrease, and the result does not prove that every center-finding algorithm is slow. The evidence package contains the complete written proof, source code and exact finite checks, including a fifty-one-vertex example. Those checks do not establish the infinite-family theorems or historical priority. This is an unrefereed Evidence Press candidate dated September twenty-first, twenty twenty-six. The paper and evidence are linked on the release page. This is an AI-generated voice summary, not additional evidence.
